newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trades twice after two days of no deals.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trades twice after two days of no deals.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures saw two trades on Wednesday morning and a healthier range of bid/offer spreads at the end of the morning session following two days when no deals were done.

October traded once for five lots, the minimum volume, at 10.80 pence a therm, up 0.125 pence from the previous settlement level. And November traded a single 10-lot deal at 12.75 pence, up 0.21 pence from Tuesday evening.

Both bids and offers were posted for the first eight months of the contract, with front month August showing a spread of 9.20/9.30 pence, straddling the settlement price of 9.27. By comparison, at the close of trade on Tuesday bids and offers were only posted on two months.

But further out some wide gaps were seen between bids and offers. January and February both saw a stand-off of a full penny a therm, between 17 and 18 pence, while March saw a huge 1.60 pence spread, bid at 12.90 pence and offered at 14.50 pence.
